name: 90/90 Hip Switches
cue: Sit on the floor, both knees bent to about 90° — one shin in front of you, the other out to the side. Keep tall and rotate your hips to swap both legs to the other side. Slow and controlled. Opens the hips with zero stress on the knee.

name: Arm Circles
cue: One arm at a time. Ten big slow circles forward, ten backward. Wakes the shoulder up before you load it.

name: Down Dog to Up Dog
cue: Hips high in an upside-down V, then sweep the chest through and forward until the arms are straight. Hold five seconds at each end.

name: World's Greatest Stretch
cue: Step one foot forward into a gentle lunge, both hands on the floor inside the front foot. Reach the inside arm up to the ceiling and turn your chest to follow it. Bring it back down, step back, switch sides. Opens hips, chest and back in one move.

name: Ankle Mobility
cue: Knee over toe, heel down.

name: Cat–Cow
cue: Flow spine flexion ↔ extension.

name: Deep Squat Rocks
cue: Sit deep, rock side to side.

name: Doorway Chest Stretch
cue: Forearm on frame, rotate away.

name: Hip CARs
cue: Slow, controlled full hip circles.

name: Hip-Flexor Stretch
cue: Tall hips, posterior tilt, per side.

name: Overhead Shoulder Stretch
cue: Lat/shoulder stretch, ribs down.

name: Thoracic Opener
cue: Open-book / quadruped reach-through.

name: Thoracic Rotations
cue: Quadruped, reach hand to ceiling.

name: Wrist Prep Rocks
cue: Rock over wrists, all directions.

name: Hollow Hold (heels down)
cue: Lie on your back with your heels resting on the floor. Lift only your shoulders off the ground and press your low back flat. Easiest version — nothing should pull on your back.

name: Incline Plank
cue: Hands on bench, body straight head to heel. Reduce bench height to progress.

name: Bear Hold
cue: Bear-crawl position held still: hands under shoulders, knees hovering an inch off the floor, back flat. Squeeze everything and hold. A held bear crawl — brutal deep-core tension.

name: Bent-Knee Hollow Hold
cue: Lift the shoulder blades off the floor, knees bent at 90°, arms extended straight back behind the ears. Low back pressed flat. The easier hollow — keeps the legs light to protect the lower back.

name: Dead Bug
cue: Lie on back, arms up, knees bent to 90°. Press the low back into the floor. Lower the opposite arm and leg toward the floor slowly, then return to center. Brace the whole time.

name: Flutter Kicks
cue: Legs straight, heels six inches off the floor, low back pressed down. Alternate small fast up-down kicks. Keep the core braced the whole set.

name: Scissor Kicks
cue: Legs straight, heels off the floor. Cross one leg over the other in a scissor motion, alternating. Low back stays glued to the floor.

name: Bodyline Drill
cue: Face down on floor. Arms straight overhead. Squeeze everything: glutes, core, quads, push armpits toward ears. Body is one rigid plank. The fundamental shape that all handstand work requires.

name: Forearm Plank
cue: Elbows under shoulders. Neutral spine. Posterior pelvic tilt. Squeeze glutes. No sagging or piking.

name: High Plank
cue: Arms straight, wrists under shoulders. Body rigid head to heel. Active shoulders — push the floor away.

name: Hollow Hold
cue: Lower back pressed flat. Ribcage closed. Arms overhead. Foundation of all gymnastics.

name: Dragon Flag Candlestick
cue: Grip a sturdy anchor behind the head. Roll the hips back, kick straight legs vertical (weight on the upper back, not neck), then lower the hips down rolling the spine one vertebra at a time. The hip-lift base.

name: Plank Leg Lift
cue: Forearm plank. Lift one leg 6 inches — squeeze glute at top. No hip rotation. Hold 2 sec. Alternate.

name: Plank Shoulder Taps
cue: High plank. Tap opposite shoulder — fight the rotation. Wider foot stance for more stability.

name: Dragon Flag (Tuck)
cue: From the vertical candlestick, knees tucked, lock the hips so torso and thighs are one rigid line and lower slowly (5-sec negative) until the lower back touches. Slow negatives (reps) OR hold parallel.

name: Elevated Feet Plank
cue: High plank with feet on bench. More load shifts to upper core and shoulders. 30-60 sec.

name: Hollow Rocks
cue: From hollow body hold, rock forward and back like a rocking chair. No momentum — all core.

name: Long-Lever Plank
cue: Forearm plank but hands extended further forward. Increases the lever arm dramatically. Pure anti-extension strength.

name: Plank Up-Downs
cue: Start in forearm plank. Press up one hand at a time to high plank, then lower back down one hand at a time. Alternate the leading arm. Fight rotation throughout.

name: RKC Plank
cue: Posterior pelvic tilt, squeeze fists and glutes hard. 10s sets are enough.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
cue: Hips must not sag at extension. Pull from abs — not hip flexors — to return.

name: Plank Bodysaw
cue: Forearm plank on sliders or socks. Slide body forward and pull back. Anti-extension at its hardest. Keep hips from sagging.

name: Squeeze-Loaded Hollow Hold
cue: Full hollow hold with a yoga block or ball squeezed between the ankles and a light plate held overhead. Squeeze hard — irradiation multiplies the load on the lower abs. Elite hollow.

name: Tuck Dragon Flag Hold
cue: Tucked, lower the rigid body until the torso hovers 2-3 inches parallel above the bench and freeze — weight on the shoulder blades and arms. Static tuck dragon flag.

name: Single Arm Plank
cue: High plank — remove one arm. Fight hard to prevent rotation. Start at 10-15 sec per side. Build from there.

name: Single-Leg Dragon Flag
cue: One leg straight (locked knee, pointed toe), the other knee tucked. Keeping a dead-rigid waistline, lower until parallel to the bench. Switch legs. Slow negatives (reps) OR hold. Bridges tuck → full.

name: Single Arm + Leg Plank
cue: One arm, opposite leg lifted. Two-point plank. Hardest plank variation. Master single arm before attempting.

name: Inverted Candle
cue: From the inverted hang, lock a straight line shoulders-to-toes (a vertical candle), then slowly lower the straight body toward horizontal, pivoting only at the shoulders. The ultimate suspension test (hanging dragon flag).

name: Walk-Up Planks
cue: Walk hands out to plank and back; long body.

name: Bicycle Crunch
cue: Lying crunch: opposite elbow to opposite knee in a pedaling motion. Slow and controlled beats fast and sloppy. Obliques + hip flexors.

name: Russian Twist
cue: Sit at 45° lean, feet off floor. Rotate torso side to side. Touch ground each side. Add weight to progress.

name: Side Plank
cue: Knees bent 90°. Hip stacked, not sagging. Free hand on hip or extended up. 30-60 sec per side.

name: Side Plank Hip Dip
cue: Full side plank: lower hip toward floor without touching, drive back up. Oblique-focused. 10-15 reps each side.

name: Side Plank Leg Raise
cue: Full side plank: raise top leg to hip height and lower with control. Abductors and obliques working simultaneously.

name: Copenhagen Plank
cue: Top leg on bench, bottom leg floating. Straight body. Insane adductor + core.

name: Jamaican Plank
cue: From high plank, rotate into star side plank (top arm + top leg raised), hold 1 sec, rotate back through center plank, then rotate to the other side. Non-stop alternating. Also called alternating star plank or rotating star plank.

name: Star Side Plank
cue: Side plank: raise top arm and top leg simultaneously into full star shape. Maximum stability demand on every plane.

name: Windshield Wipers
cue: Hang from bar. Legs together, rotate side to side. Oblique gold.

name: Bird Dog
cue: On all fours. Extend the right arm forward and the left leg straight back at the same time. Hold 2 sec without letting the hips rotate, then switch sides. Anti-rotation control.

name: Bear Hold Taps
cue: From a static bear hold (knees hovering an inch off the floor), slowly tap one hand to the opposite shoulder, then switch. Keep the hips dead-even — no rotation. Anti-rotation under load.

name: Bear Limb Lift
cue: Hold the hovering bear position and lift just one hand OR one foot slightly off the ground, hold briefly, return, then alternate. Two-point stability — fight the urge to shift your weight.

name: Bear Opposing Limb Lift
cue: From the bear hold, lift the opposing arm and leg (right arm + left leg) at once, hold 2-3 sec, then switch. The hardest bear variation — maximal anti-rotation and balance.

name: Plank Opposite Arm + Leg
cue: High plank: extend opposite arm and leg simultaneously. Hold 2 sec at top. Anti-rotation + anti-extension in one movement. Bird-dog in plank position.

name: KOT Calf Raise
cue: Knees-over-toes calf, deep stretch.

name: Foot-Supported L-Sit
cue: Beginner L-sit: hands pressing down on the floor (or parallettes), knees bent or heels lightly touching the floor. Press the shoulders down and lift the chest. Build the compression before going feet-up.

name: Alternating Single-Leg L-Sit
cue: Glutes lifted, arms locked. Lift one foot off the floor, hold a few seconds, tap it down, then lift the other — march the legs (bent-knee or straight-leg style). Builds toward zero foot support.

name: Seated Knee Tuck Raises
cue: Sit on floor or parallettes, hands beside hips, arms straight. Pull knees to chest explosively, hold 1-2s at top. Lower with control. Builds the strength needed for L-sit and press to handstand.

name: Pike Compression Lifts
cue: Seated on floor, legs straight. Actively flex hip flexors to fold chest toward legs. Each rep is a muscular contraction — not gravity. THE L-sit/V-sit builder.

name: Straddle V-Up
cue: Sit up opening both straight legs wide into a V straddle, reaching the hands through the center to the floor or ankles. Wide legs shorten the lever — easier than a closed-leg V-up.

name: Tuck L-Sit
cue: Knees tucked to chest in L-sit position. Build to 10s before extending legs.

name: Tuck V-Sit Hold
cue: From parallel bars or floor. Arms locked, scapula depressed. Tuck knees to chest, feet OFF floor. Build to 3x15s before extending legs.

name: Seated Straight Leg Raises
cue: Sit on floor or parallettes, arms straight beside hips, scapula depressed. Raise straight legs up as high as possible. Lower with control. Pure compression strength and active hamstring flexibility.

name: Straddle Leg Lifts
cue: Sit, legs straddled wide. Lift both legs in straddle — keeping knees straight. Develops active compression + straddle flexibility simultaneously. Key for press to handstand.

name: Hollow-to-V-Sit Snap-Up
cue: From a low full hollow hold (heels 6 inches up), snap up into a full V-up touching the toes, then drop back into a rock-solid frozen hollow — no floor rest. Elite eccentric core control.

name: L-Sit Hold
cue: Arm lockout, depress scapulae, legs parallel to floor. Build tuck first.

name: One-Leg L-Sit
cue: From a tuck L-sit (glutes off floor), keep one knee tucked and extend the other leg dead straight out parallel to the floor, toes pointed. Switch legs. Hold, or do dynamic kick-outs. Bridges tuck → full L-sit.

name: Straddle L-Sit
cue: Legs spread wide in straddle rather than parallel. Easier to hold than strict L-sit. Good stepping stone to V-sit.

name: One-Leg V-Sit
cue: From the high tuck V-sit (leaning back, knees high), keep one knee tucked to the shoulder and kick the other leg straight up high toward the ceiling, above head height. Alternate legs.

name: Ring L-Sit
cue: L-sit on rings. Fight rotation — rings want to turn inward. Much harder than parallettes due to instability. Builds serious core and lat strength.

name: Straddle V-Sit
cue: Lean the torso back, push the hips up, launch both straight legs wide into a high V straddle, knees locked. Wide legs shorten the lever — the gateway to the full V-sit.

name: V-Sit
cue: Legs above horizontal. Lean torso slightly back to counterbalance. Active compression.

name: Superman
cue: Prone on floor. Simultaneously raise arms, chest, and legs off the ground. Hold 2 sec. Lower with control. Great lower back and posterior chain activation.

name: Crunch
cue: Lie on back, knees bent. Curl the shoulder blades off the floor by flexing the abs — don't yank the neck. Lower with control. Top-ab spinal flexion.

name: Lying Knee Tuck
cue: Lie on back, hands by hips or under the glutes. Draw the knees toward the chest, curling the hips slightly off the floor. Lower-ab entry movement.

name: Reverse Crunch
cue: Knees at 90°. Curl the pelvis up toward the ribs — lift the hips off the floor using the lower abs, not a leg swing. Slow eccentric.

name: Sit-Up
cue: Full range — shoulder blades up to the knees and back down. Knees bent, feet planted. Drive through the abs, not momentum. Classic top-ab builder.

name: Toe Touch Crunch
cue: Legs straight up toward the ceiling. Reach the hands toward the toes, curling the upper back off the floor. Squeeze the upper abs at the top.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
cue: From dead hang, pull knees to chest. Control the descent. No swinging.

name: Hollow Body Crunch
cue: From a full hollow hold, crunch the ribs toward the pelvis a few inches and return without losing the hollow line. Constant tension on the deep core — a hollow-position crunch.

name: Lying Leg Raise
cue: Lie flat, legs straight. Raise the legs to vertical keeping them straight, then lower slowly without letting the heels touch. Hands under the glutes to protect the low back.

name: Tuck-Up
cue: Lie flat, arms overhead, legs hovering. Crunch up while pulling both knees deeply into the chest, reach the hands past the feet at the peak balancing on the glutes, then open back to flat. The bent-knee V-up.

name: Single-Leg V-Up
cue: Sit up dynamically throwing ONE straight leg up, reaching both hands to touch that foot at the peak. Lower with control, alternate sides. Half the lower-body load of a full V-up.

name: V-Up
cue: Lie flat, arms overhead. Simultaneously lift legs and torso to meet in a V, hands toward feet. Lower under control — no slamming down.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
cue: No swing. Posterior pelvic tilt at top. Control the descent. Legs straight.

name: Toes-to-Bar
cue: Posterior pelvic tilt. Touch toes to bar. Minimize kip. Control descent.

name: Hanging Inverted Hold
cue: Pull the toes to the bar then keep tilting the hips back until the feet point at the ceiling — body upside down, tucked or straight. Depress the scapula hard. Balance shifts to the upper back and deep core.

name: Bird Dog Crunch
cue: Extend, then draw elbow-to-knee under body.

name: Banded Pull-Aparts
cue: Straight arms, squeeze blades.

name: Incline Row
cue: High bar, body fairly upright. Row chest to bar.

name: Australian Pull-Up
cue: Bar at hip height, straight body, chest to bar. Feet forward = harder.

name: Ring Row
cue: Neutral grip, squeeze blades.

name: Wide Inverted Row
cue: Wide grip inverted row — upper back and lats.

name: Feet-Elevated Ring Row
cue: Feet up on a box — nearly horizontal, much harder.

name: Archer Row
cue: One arm pulls, the other stays straight out to the side.

name: Single-Arm Ring Row
cue: One arm, feet forward. Fight the rotation.

name: Wall Push-Up
cue: Hands on wall at chest height, feet a step back. Body straight. Press into wall, control the return. The further your feet, the harder.

name: Incline Push-Up
cue: Hands on elevated surface. Great entry-level push pattern. Elbows 45°. Chest to bench.

name: Knee Push-Up
cue: From knees, hands shoulder-width, body straight from knees to head. Chest to floor. Lock arms at top. No hip pike — this is a real push-up scaled.

name: Shorties
cue: Bottom-half partial push-ups — chest near floor to mid-range, no lockout at top. Continuous tension, deep stretch on the chest, no rest. Alternative: top-half pulses (upper 50%, no chest touch) — different stimulus, less stretch. Both = killer pump tools after full push-ups.

name: Bench Dip
cue: Hands behind on bench, feet on floor or elevated. Full depth. Great entry-level dip.

name: Dip Support Hold
cue: Top of the dip position — arms locked, shoulders depressed and packed, body upright. Hold full bodyweight without bending arms. The entry test for dip work. Build 30-60s before attempting reps.

name: Push-ups
cue: Elbows 45°, chest to floor, protract fully at top. Active core throughout.

name: Banded Dip
cue: Loop a resistance band over the parallel bars, knees rest in the band loop. The band assists the press out of the bottom. Choose band tension so you can do 5-8 reps unbroken. Progress by switching to a lighter band.

name: Decline Push-Up
cue: Feet elevated, lead with chest. Straight body from head to heels.

name: Dip Bottom Hold
cue: Bottom of the dip — shoulder below elbow, controlled tension. Hold here to build strength at the hardest position. Start at 5-10s holds, build to 30s.

name: Dip Negative
cue: Start at the top of the dip (arms locked). Lower yourself slowly — 4-5 seconds down to the bottom. Step off and reset. Eccentric work builds the strength to press up. 3-5 negatives per set.

name: Hindu Push-Up
cue: Start in pike. Arc chest close to ground forward into upward dog, push to lockout. Reverse the arc back to pike. Not a push-up — it's a full shoulder arc wave. Control the spine extension at the top.

name: Ring Support Hold
cue: Straight arms, rings turned out at bottom (RTO). Shoulders depressed and packed. Build to 30-60s before ring dips.

name: Dead-Stop Push-up
cue: Lower all the way to the floor. Lift hands off — full tension release. Reset. Press from zero. No stretch reflex, no momentum. Every rep is a fresh max effort. Brutally effective for pure chest strength.

name: Diamond Push-Up
cue: Hands form diamond, elbows track back, squeeze triceps hard at lockout.

name: Dip
cue: Slight lean for chest, upright for triceps. Full depth. No shoulder shrug.

name: Elephant Walk
cue: Start in pike/downward dog. Walk hands backward toward feet, keeping legs as straight as possible and hips high. Alternate hand steps. Bridges pike strength to press to handstand.

name: Navy Seal Push-Up (3 pump)
cue: At the bottom of each push-up, do 3 small partial pumps (chest stays an inch off floor) before pressing back to lockout. 1 set = 3 pumps + 1 full rep. Time-under-tension at the hardest position. Brutal for chest endurance.

name: Ring Push-Up
cue: Keep rings close, turn out (RTO) at lockout. Serratus fires hard.

name: T-Rotation Push-Up
cue: Push-up, then rotate body into a side plank and raise top arm straight up forming a T. Alternate sides. Push + anti-rotation in one movement.

name: Archer Complex
cue: Alternating: unilateral ring row right → push-up → ring row left = 1 rep. Scapular control on each row. Hips square. The push-up is the controlled reset between rows. Pull elbow back — not out.

name: Ring Dip Support Hold
cue: Locked out on the rings, rings turned out, shoulders down. Stillness is the whole exercise.

name: Straight Bar Dip
cue: Support over a straight bar, lean forward slightly, lower until the chest reaches the bar. Harder on the shoulder than parallel bars — earn it.

name: Archer Push-Up
cue: Shift weight to one arm, other arm straight for balance. Hips square.

name: Half One-Arm Push-Up
cue: Working arm shoulder-width, free hand on a low box (so the body angle is steeper than incline but easier than full one-arm). Slow descent on one arm only. The box absorbs less weight as it lowers.

name: Ring Dip
cue: Full lockout with RTO. Rings tight to body. Control the descent.

name: Ring Dip + Knee Raise
cue: Full ring dip → hold at top → compress knees to chest. Shoulders packed. RTO at lockout. The knee raise is active compression — not a swing. Link the push and core as one unit.

name: Assisted One-Arm Push-Up
cue: Use a band looped overhead, hooked under the chest to unload some bodyweight, OR free hand resting LIGHTLY on a low surface for balance only (not bearing weight). Working arm does the work.

name: Bulgarian Dip
cue: On rings. From the top of a ring dip, rotate the rings outward and turn the palms forward at the top (Bulgarian press). Adds rotational shoulder stability + tricep load. Slow tempo only.

name: One-Arm Push-Up
cue: Feet wide, hips square. 3s descent. Master archer push-up first.

name: Russian Dip
cue: Parallel bar dip. At the bottom, lower onto your forearms (forearms touch the bars). Press back up to the dip start — drive through forearms then hands. Brutal triceps + shoulder control. Start with 1-3 reps, build slowly.

name: Weighted Deep Ring Push-Up
cue: Deep ROM, turn rings out at top. (Phase-2 push anchor)

name: Weighted Dip
cue: Full depth, controlled, lean forward.

name: Glute Bridge
cue: Heels close to your bum, toes up. Drive through the heels and squeeze hard at the top for a full second. Ribs down — the glutes lift, not the lower back.

name: High Pull-Up
cue: Pull to lower-chest / waist height — the height a muscle-up needs.

name: Banded Glute Bridge
cue: Drive knees out, squeeze top.

name: Banded Lateral Walks
cue: Band at knees, stay low, continuous side-steps.

name: Nordic Curl
cue: Control the eccentric; progress ROM → load.

name: Single-Leg Bridge
cue: Hips level, full extension.

name: Sliding Hamstring Curl
cue: Hips up, slow eccentric.

name: Touchdown Squat
cue: Knees-over-toes, controlled reach.

name: Tibialis Raise
cue: Toes up against wall, full ROM.

name: Bench Squat
cue: Stand in front of a bench, feet a bit wider than the hips. Sit back until you touch it lightly, then stand. Touch — do not drop onto it.

name: Bodyweight Squat
cue: Feet about shoulder width, sit down between the hips. Hip crease below the knee, chest tall, drive through the whole foot.

name: Wall Sit
cue: Back flat on the wall, slide down until your thighs are somewhere comfortable — the higher you stay, the easier on the knee. Hold still and breathe.

name: Assisted Reverse Nordic Curl
cue: Knees-over-toes eccentric; assist with band or hands.

name: Horse Stance
cue: Thighs parallel, isometric hold.

name: Sissy Squat
cue: Knees forward, lean back — quad-focused. (future anchor)

name: Slant Squat Pulses
cue: Heels elevated, small quad pulses.

name: Slant-Board Squat
cue: Tempo 311, full depth, heels raised.

name: Straight-Arm Lat Raise
cue: Straight arms, drive the bar down / hips up with the lats only. The front-lever base.

name: Band-Assisted Front Lever
cue: Band under the hips supports the lever. Thinner band to progress.

name: Front Lever Tuck
cue: Gentle while forearm heals. Posterior tilt.

name: Skin the Cat
cue: Controlled German-hang rotation; decompress.

name: Tuck Front Lever Raise
cue: From dead hang, pull dynamically up into a tuck front lever, lower under control.

name: Adv-Tuck FL Raise
cue: Same raise, advanced-tuck position.

name: Advanced-Tuck Front Lever
cue: Open the tuck — hips extended, flat back, knees still bent.

name: German Hang
cue: Inverted hang, shoulders fully extended behind. Mobility + strength.

name: Single-Leg FL Raise
cue: Raise with one leg extended straight.

name: Single-Leg Front Lever
cue: One leg straight, one tucked. Switch sides.

name: Skin the Cat to Front Support
cue: Pull through the German hang back up to a front support.

name: Front Lever Row
cue: From a front-lever line, row the body up to the bar. Elite back.

name: Ice Cream Maker
cue: From a front lever, pull to an inverted/pull-up top. Front-lever-to-bar.

name: Straddle FL Raise
cue: Raise into a straddle front lever.

name: Straddle Front Lever
cue: Legs straight and wide — shortens the lever vs full.

name: Front Lever Pull-Up
cue: Pull-up while holding the front-lever line. Extreme.

name: Full FL Raise
cue: Raise into a full front lever — elite.

name: Full Front Lever
cue: Body dead straight and horizontal. The goal hold.

name: Frog Stand
cue: Hands shoulder-width, knees resting on elbows/triceps. Lean forward and lift feet. First real planche shape — accessible to beginners. Build to 30s.

name: Planche Lean
cue: Arms locked, lean forward until shoulders over or past wrists. Go further each week.

name: Frog Planche
cue: Between Tuck and Advanced Tuck. Knees rest lightly on the outside of your elbows while leaning forward. Slowly pull knees away from the arms as you gain strength. The bridge that lets you load planche torque without full bodyweight commitment.

name: Open Tuck Planche
cue: Knees off the chest, knees still bent. Lower back should flatten completely — hips no longer protected by the tuck. The jump from this to Adv Tuck is where most people stall; do not skip it.

name: Planche Lean Raises
cue: Start in a standard planche lean. Press hard through your shoulders WHILE walking or sliding your feet forward — forcing your hips to elevate until your toes lightly float off the floor. The dynamic version of planche lean that introduces the hip lift.

name: Tuck Planche Hold
cue: Wrists turned out, shoulders over wrists, max protraction, knees tight to chest.

name: Adv. Tuck Planche
cue: Back flat, legs tuck below hips. 5s max holds with full rest.

name: L-Sit Push-Back to Planche
cue: Start in L-sit or tuck sit on parallettes. Fluidly push hips backward and upward through a tuck planche, aiming to extend into straddle or full planche for a brief 1-2 second hold. Trains the dynamic entry to planche.

name: Pseudo Planche Push-Up
cue: Hands turned out, lean forward — shoulders over wrists. Maintain hollow body.

name: Semi-Straddle Planche
cue: Also called Closed Straddle. Legs spread wide BUT knees bent at 90°. Reduces lever length while training hip abduction. The final bridge before Full Straddle.

name: Single-Leg Planche
cue: From an Adv Tuck, extend exactly ONE leg straight back; keep the other tightly tucked. Alternate legs per set. This bridges the gap from Adv Tuck directly to Straddle Planche by training one half of the lever at a time.

name: Straight-Arm Dip (Rings)
cue: From RTO ring support hold, lean shoulders forward over (or past) the rings. Arms stay LOCKED straight throughout. Descend the body angle by leaning, not by bending arms. Pure straight-arm scapular + anterior shoulder strength — direct planche prep. Hold 3-10s leans, 3-5 sets.

name: 90-Degree HSPU Negative
cue: Slowly lower from a handstand while "seesawing" the body horizontal until you catch a bent-arm planche position (head + chest at 90°). The fusion of HSPU eccentric with planche bottom position. Multi-year skill.

name: Handstand to Planche Negative
cue: Start in a solid handstand. Arms locked. Slowly lower the body down through straddle or full layout, attempting to catch and freeze the movement right at the horizontal planche line. The eccentric forces the CNS to adapt to full planche load.

name: Straddle Planche
cue: Legs straddled. Maintain hollow body. Years of work to reach here.

name: Full 90-Degree HSPU
cue: Lower from handstand into a bent-arm horizontal hold (the 90° planche position) and press back up to vertical handstand. Combines full HSPU range with planche-tier shoulder strength. The pinnacle of vertical+horizontal push fusion. Endpoint.

name: Full Planche
cue: Full straight-body planche hold. Legs together, body parallel to floor, shoulders over (and past) wrists. The pinnacle of straight-arm pushing strength. 3-5 second hold = elite. Multi-year skill — wrist conditioning mandatory.

name: Planche Push-Up
cue: From a full planche hold, lower body to chest-to-floor maintaining the planche position (no leg drop), press back to the planche. Hardest bodyweight push movement that exists in calisthenics. 1-3 strict reps = elite.

name: Active Hang
cue: Shoulders packed, ribs down.

name: Dead Hang
cue: Passive full hang. Decompress the spine, build grip.

name: Scapular Pull-ups
cue: Depress/retract scaps, arms straight.

name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
cue: Band under feet/knee removes weight. Step down band thickness to progress.

name: Negative Pull-Up
cue: Jump to the top, lower 3-5s. Builds the pull eccentrically.

name: Chin-up
cue: Supinated, full ROM.

name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
cue: Palms facing — kindest on the elbows and forearm.

name: Pull-Up
cue: Dead-hang start, chin over bar, controlled descent.

name: Towel Hang
cue: Hang from towels. Grip endurance.

name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
cue: Wider than shoulders — lat emphasis.

name: Commando Pull-Up
cue: Straddle the bar, pull side to side, alternate lead hand.

name: Explosive Chin-up
cue: Pull fast — chest toward bar.

name: Explosive Pull-Up
cue: Pull as high and fast as possible — power for the muscle-up.

name: Pull-Over
cue: Pull, then roll the hips over the bar to support. Transition builder.

name: Towel Pull-Up
cue: Pull-ups gripping two towels — brutal grip and forearm.

name: Band-Assisted Muscle-Up
cue: Band assists the transition. Grease the whole movement.

name: Chest-to-Bar Pull-Up
cue: Pull higher — sternum to the bar. Muscle-up prep.

name: L-Sit Pull-up
cue: Hold the L, full pull — back + core.

name: Negative Muscle-Up (Bar)
cue: Start on top of the bar, lower slowly through the transition.

name: One-Arm Hang
cue: Hang from one arm 5-10s. Builds toward one-arm pulling.

name: Weighted Chin-Up
cue: Supinated (forearm-smart). Full ROM.

name: Archer Pull-Up
cue: One arm bends, the other stays straight. Shift side to side.

name: Around-the-World Pull-Up
cue: Arc side to side over the bar in a U shape.

name: False-Grip Pull-Up
cue: Wrists over the rings (false grip). The ring muscle-up gateway.

name: Typewriter Pull-Up
cue: At the top, slide side to side keeping the chin above the bar.

name: Muscle-Up (Bar)
cue: Explosive pull, transition elbows over the bar, press out.

name: Muscle-Up (Rings)
cue: False grip, deep transition, press to support on rings.

name: One-Arm Negative Pull-Up
cue: One arm, slow lower only. Assist gently with the free hand.

name: One-Arm Pull-Up
cue: The elite pull — full range, one arm.

name: Pike Hold
cue: Inverted V position, straight arms, push floor away. Hold position. Builds wrist endurance and shoulder overhead strength.

name: Pike Pulses
cue: Sit in pike (legs straight together). Actively pulse torso DOWN toward legs using hip flexors only — not gravity bounce. 20-30 reps. Key compression warm-up before handstand or L-sit work.

name: Feet on Wall 90 Degree
cue: Hands on floor ~1 foot from wall, feet walked up the wall to hip height — body forms a 90° angle. Hold position with shoulders stacked. The L-shape primes the overhead press pattern for HSPU work.

name: Pike Lean
cue: From pike, shift shoulders FORWARD over wrists. No balance assist — pure strength. The further you lean, the harder it gets.

name: Pike Push-Up
cue: Hips high, head goes through arms at bottom, press overhead.

name: Chest-to-Wall Handstand Hold
cue: Face the wall. Walk up into handstand with the chest, thighs and feet near the wall (NOT the back). Locked elbows, elevated scapula. Only the feet touch the wall — body straight line. Trains the same alignment as freestanding handstand without the balance demand.

name: Elevated Pike Lean
cue: Feet elevated on bench. Pike lean forward — more load through the arms due to elevation.

name: Elevated Pike Push-Up
cue: Feet elevated on bench in pike position. Press overhead. Closer to handstand angle than floor pike push-up.

name: Handstand Kick-Ups
cue: Practice the dynamic entry to freestanding handstand. Kick up, find balance briefly, come down. Reps = entries. Use wall nearby for safety.

name: Wall Walk
cue: Start in push-up position. Walk feet up wall and hands in toward wall simultaneously until chest is close to wall. Walk back down with control.

name: Back-to-Wall Handstand Hold
cue: Kick up facing AWAY from wall. Heels lightly touch wall. Good entry to handstand balance work.

name: Pike Lean on Parallettes
cue: Parallettes allow DEEPER lean = greater forward lean angle = more horizontal load. Far harder than floor version. Directly bridges to planche and handstand strength.

name: Wall Handstand
cue: Straight line ears-hips-heels. Active shoulders (push floor away). Gaze at floor.

name: Wall Handstand Hold
cue: Chest to wall version: hands ~6in from wall. Hollow body, active shoulders. Chest-to-wall is harder than back-to-wall — less arch, more true handstand position.

name: Chest-to-Wall Deficit HSPU
cue: Hands on parallettes facing the wall, chest-to-wall handstand position. Lower your head BELOW the level of your hands (the deficit). Press back up to lockout. Builds the deepest range of motion needed for full HSPU.

name: Wall HSPU
cue: Hands shoulder-width, head to floor, press to full lockout. Ribs closed.

name: Freestanding HS
cue: Balance with finger pressure. Micro-wrist adjustments. Breathe and relax.

name: Handstand Push-Up
cue: Freestanding handstand push-up. From a balanced freestanding handstand, lower head to floor under control, press back to full lockout. No wall, no kick assist. The HSPU benchmark for elite calisthenics. Build to 5 strict.

name: Press to Handstand
cue: From standing pike (forward fold), press straight into freestanding handstand without jumping or kicking. Pure compression + straight-arm pressing strength. Combines straddle/pike flexibility with planche-tier shoulder strength. Multi-year goal.

name: Deep Parallette Pike Push-Up
cue: Hips stacked, deep ROM off parallettes.

name: Freestanding Attempts
cue: Kick to balance, ride it as long as you can, bail safely.

name: Kick-Up Practice
cue: Freestanding entries — find the balance point, bail to a cartwheel.

name: Kettlebell Halo
cue: Hold the bell upside down by the horns at the chest. Circle it slowly around the head, close to the skull. Five each way, ribs down.

name: Prying Goblet Squat
cue: Hold the bell at the chest and sit into the deepest squat you have. Use the elbows to push the knees out, and rock. A stretch, not a set.

name: Goblet March
cue: Bell at the chest, stand tall. Lift one knee to hip height, hold a beat, put it down. A plank you do standing up.

name: Suitcase Carry
cue: One bell, one hand, hanging by your side. Walk tall and resist the tilt — staying vertical is the exercise, not the walking.

name: Prone Y-T-W Raise
cue: Face down on an incline bench, arms hanging, thumbs up. Raise the arms into a Y overhead, lower. Then straight out to a T, lower. Then bent into a W, lower. That is one rep. No weight or very light — this is for the small muscles that hold your shoulders back.

name: Chest-Supported Rear-Delt Row
cue: Chest on the incline bench, dumbbells hanging. Row them out WIDE with your elbows flared out to the sides, up toward your chest — not tucked to your ribs. The wide elbow path is what makes it hit the back of the shoulders. Squeeze, lower slow.

name: Seal Row
cue: Prone on a bench, row the dumbbells — no momentum, pure back.

name: Single-Arm Row
cue: Square hips, drive elbow back, full stretch.

name: Kettlebell Floor Press
cue: On your back, knees bent, bell in one hand at the chest. Press to over the shoulder, not over the face. The floor stops the elbow — touch, pause, press.

name: Push-Ups on Dumbbells
cue: Hands gripping two dumbbells set on the floor so your wrists stay straight. Body in one line, chest down between them, press back up.

name: Full Burpee
cue: Squat → hands → jump back → chest to floor (full push-up) → jump feet in → squat → explosive jump with arms overhead. One fluid motion. Land soft every rep. No shortcuts — full range is the entire point.

name: Bottoms-Up KB Hold
cue: Kettlebell upside-down at shoulder, bell pointing to ceiling. Wrist neutral, elbow tucked. The bell wants to flop — your grip + shoulder stabilizers fight for the line. 20–40 sec each hand. Brutal for shoulder stability + grip.

name: Diamond Push-Up on Kettlebell
cue: Diamond grip on a single KB handle. Lower deep — the KB elevates your hands giving extra ROM. Elbows track tight. Squeeze hard at top. Bell stability adds a hidden challenge.

name: Navy Seal Burpee
cue: 3 push-ups at bottom of each burpee, then jump + clap. Punishing and effective.

name: Devil's Press
cue: Burpee down, chest touches floor. Explosive hip hinge to snatch both DBs overhead in one motion. Arms stay straight on the swing up. Control the descent — don't drop.

name: Man-Maker
cue: Push-up → row right → row left → feet jump in → clean → squat → overhead press. One rep = all 7 steps. Hips square during rows. Drive from legs into the press.

name: Kettlebell Deadlift
cue: Bell on the floor between the feet. Push the hips back until your hands reach it, back flat, shins near vertical. Stand by driving the floor away.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
cue: Push your hips back and slide the dumbbells down the front of your legs. Knees stay almost straight. Stop when you feel the stretch behind your thighs, then stand tall.

name: Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
cue: Start standing. Push the hips back and slide the bell down the thighs, knees soft and staying soft. Go until the hamstrings stop you.

name: Kettlebell Swing
cue: Snap the hips — the arms are just rope. The bell floats up to chest height from your hips driving forward, not from lifting with your shoulders. Start at 12–16 kg.

name: Kettlebell High Pull
cue: Swing as normal, then guide the elbow high and back as the bell floats. The hips still do all the work — the arm only steers.

name: Dumbbell Swing
cue: Hip snap, not a squat. (KB→DB)

name: Leg Swings
cue: Front-back then lateral, controlled.

name: Single-Leg RDL
cue: Hinge on one leg, square hips, hamstring stretch.

name: Fast March
cue: Knees high, arms driving, stay light. Both feet never leave the floor at once — this is the no-impact way to raise a heart rate.

name: Standing High-Knee March
cue: March on the spot, driving each knee up to hip height. Stay tall. No jumping, no impact — knee-friendly swap for mountain climbers.

name: Farmer's Carry (no straps)
cue: A dumbbell in each hand, no straps — grip is the point. Walk tall, shoulders back, 30-40 m. Set them down when the round is done, not when your grip fails. If they slip early, go lighter. Start 40-50 lb per hand.

name: Mountain Climbers
cue: From a high plank, drive the knees to the chest one at a time, fast. Hips stay low, shoulders stacked over hands, core braced. Multi-purpose: plank-hold core + shoulder/push stability + conditioning — used across core, push, and conditioning work.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
cue: Front-foot loaded, knee tracks toes.

name: Burpee
cue: Squat-jump back-push-up-jump forward-jump + clap overhead. Rhythm is everything.

name: Goblet Squat
cue: Elbows inside knees, upright torso.

name: Jump Squats
cue: Explode up, soft landing, reset.

name: Jumping Pull-Up
cue: Assist the concentric with a small jump, control the descent.

name: Burpee Pull-Up
demands: wrist-extension, deep-knee-flexion, grip, hang, impact, floor-to-stand
cue: Full burpee directly below the bar. Use the jump momentum to flow into the pull-up — don't pause between. Pull to chin over bar. Land softly on descent. One continuous fluid motion.

name: Kettlebell Overhead Press
cue: Bell racked on the forearm, wrist straight. Press up and slightly back until the arm is by the ear. Ribs down; the lower back does not help.

name: Turkish Get-Up
cue: Eyes on the bell every second of the movement. 7 steps up, 7 down. Never rush a step. Drive through heel not knee on the lunge. Wrist locked and packed throughout the entire movement.

name: Turkish Get-Up
cue: Learn it in halves with no bell for the first two weeks. Every position is a stop; nothing flows until every stop is solid.

name: Deep Squat Hold + Chest Opening
cue: Hold a rack upright or straps and sink into a squat as deep as feels fine — never into pain. Reach the free arm up and behind you and let your chest turn to follow your hand. Swap arms.

name: Down Dog to Up Dog (hands on bar)
cue: Same movement with your hands on a hip-height bar instead of the floor. Much easier on the wrists and shoulders.

name: Side Plank (hand on bar)
cue: One hand on a hip-height bar, feet on the floor, body in a straight line. The higher the bar, the easier it is.

name: Cable Rear-Delt Fly
cue: Cable set at shoulder height. Grab the handle with the opposite hand so the cable crosses your body, arm almost straight. Pull it out and across, away from your body. Constant tension the whole way. One arm at a time.

name: Chest-Supported Row
cue: Chest stays flat on the pad the whole set. Row to your ribs, pause a beat, lower slowly. The pad does the cheating for you.

name: Face Pull
cue: Rope at head height. Pull it toward your forehead and let your hands split apart at the end. Light weight, slow, feel it between the shoulder blades.

name: Reverse Fly (chest-supported)
cue: Chest flat on an incline bench, a light dumbbell in each hand hanging down. Arms almost straight, raise them out to the sides like opening your arms wide. Squeeze the back of your shoulders at the top, lower slowly. Light weight — this is never a heavy movement.

name: Seated Cable Row
cue: Chest up, pull the handle to your belly and squeeze your shoulder blades together. Do not lean back to move the weight.

name: Bent-Over Row
cue: Hinge over, flat back, row to the ribs. DB or barbell.

name: Chest Press Machine
cue: Set the seat so the handles sit level with the middle of your chest. Press out, control the way back. Do not lock out hard.

name: Lateral Raise
cue: Light dumbbells. Raise them out to the sides up to shoulder height, elbows soft. Lower slowly. This one is never heavy.

name: Triceps Pushdown
cue: Elbows glued to your sides. Push the bar or rope down until your arms are straight, then let it come back up slowly.

name: Assisted Dip (machine)
cue: Kneel or stand on the pad — the machine takes weight off you. Lean forward a little, lower until your upper arms are level with the floor, press back up. Log the ASSIST weight: lower is stronger.

name: DB Preacher Curl
cue: Use a preacher bench (or any padded incline). Isolate the bicep — curl with maximum tension and a controlled lower. Focus on the BOTTOM lockout — that is where the bicep tendon takes load. Specifically conditions the bicep tendon against hyperextension injuries that planche straight-arm pressure causes. Bulletproofs the elbow for planche work.

name: Straight Bar Push-Up
cue: Hands on parallettes or a fixed barbell. Greater depth than floor — chest drops well below hand level. Full scapular protraction at top. Narrow grip, elbows at 45°. Excellent shoulder health and chest stimulus.

name: Zanetti DB Press
cue: Lie back on a bench. Hold dumbbells with arms STRAIGHT (elbows locked) at hip level. Raise the weights up to a 45° angle above the hips, then lower slowly. Replicates the exact straight-arm shoulder flexion required for planche. ALTERNATIVE: anchor a resistance band low and pull with straight arms to the same 45° endpoint — same pattern, scalable load.

name: Bench Press
cue: Shoulder blades pinned to the bench, feet down. Bar to the sternum, elbows about 45 degrees, press to lockout.

name: Hip Abduction Machine
cue: Pads on the outside of your knees. Push your knees apart, pause, come back slowly. Sit up tall.

name: Hip Adduction Machine
cue: Flip the pads to the inside of your knees. Squeeze your knees together, pause, let them open back out slowly.

name: 45-Degree Back Extension
cue: Pad just below your hip bones. Bend at the hips and come back up until your body is one straight line — do not arch past that.

name: Deadlift
cue: Brace, push floor away, neutral spine.

name: Hip Thrust
cue: Chin tucked, full lockout, glute squeeze.

name: Romanian Deadlift
cue: Hinge, soft knees, hamstring stretch.

name: Banded Terminal Knee Extension
cue: Band around the back of your knee, anchored in front. Straighten the knee against the band and squeeze the thigh. Tiny range, big effect — knee-friendly.

name: Spanish Squat
cue: Thick band looped behind your knees and anchored in front of you. Sit back against the band and hold. Great for calming a cranky knee down.

name: Back Squat
cue: Bar on the back, brace, sit between the hips. Hip crease below the knee, knees tracking over the toes.

name: Straight-Arm DB Fly
cue: Standing or slightly leaning forward, hold light DBs at sides with arms locked straight. Raise dumbbells HORIZONTALLY out to the sides while maintaining strict scapular protraction (push the floor away). Keep the path of movement near your waistline — simulates planche load through the same shoulder angle. ALTERNATIVE: use a band anchored at hip height — pull straight out to the side with same form.

name: Barbell Curl
cue: Elbows pinned to your sides. Curl up, lower all the way down under control. If your back is swinging, the bar is too heavy.

name: Lat Pulldown
cue: Sit tall, pull the bar to your upper chest and lead with your elbows, not your hands. Let it back up slowly.

name: Chin-Up Top Hold (assisted machine)
cue: Palms facing you. Use the assist machine to get your chin above the bar, then just hold there. Chest up, shoulders down. Log the ASSIST weight: lower is stronger.

name: DB Pullover (on bench)
cue: Lie back on the bench holding one dumbbell over your chest, elbows slightly bent and fixed. Lower the dumbbell back to about head level only — feel the stretch across your lats and ribs, not deep in the shoulder. Pull it back over your chest. Start light, 20-25 lb.

name: Shoulder Press Machine
cue: Press straight overhead, ribs down so you do not arch your back. Lower until your hands are about ear height.

name: DB Shoulder Press
cue: Sit tall, a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height. Press straight overhead, ribs down so you do not arch your back. Lower back to ear height under control.

name: Overhead Press
cue: Standing and strict. Ribs down, squeeze the glutes, press until the arms are by the ears. No leg drive.
